what: One live run on second-project: GitLab's Developer Flow implements an issue the owner wrote, the card runs, the merge request is merged. Times from the GitLab API (UTC).

issue.title: greet.py: print the greeting in green when run from a terminal

auto_start_test.question: Does the card trigger's 'merge request created' condition start the card on a merge request the Developer Flow opened? GitLab shows the person who started the flow as its author.
auto_start_test.setup: card-two trigger 3136367 set to events [assign reviewer, merge request] with filter action=created at 17:35 UTC; set back to [assign reviewer] at 17:56 UTC
auto_start_test.card_started_by: a person requesting review from the card account

timeline: assigns #6 to duo-developer (the Developer Flow starts)
opens draft !6; GitLab shows the owner as author
itemator job succeeds (pipeline started by the flow's service account)
requests review from the card account (no card had started by itself)
no extras; issue and change have the same author, so the card asks a second person to read #6 and labels itemator::second-reader
comments on #6: 'Read #6 and the change, fine to merge'
limits: The issue was written by us to be small; the agent added nothing beyond it, so no thread was answered in this run.
The second reader is the owner's second account.
credits: not yet metered (the meter lags about 18 hours); estimate in the war-room ledger
